job.title: Private Partnerships & Philanthropy Assistant (Renewable Contract, LICA5)
job.description:
Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is recruiting a Senior Private Partnerships & Philanthropy (PPH) Assistant, carrying an external title of “Assistant PPH Manager”, will focus on developing and strengthening long-term partnerships with companies, foundations, and private philanthropists (PPH donors).

This position is a UNOPS position with a contract which is renewable each calendar year.

Requirements:
· Education
- Completion of Tertiary Education, degree is desirable in Communications, Marketing, Economics, Journalism, International Relations, Business Administration, Management, Social Sciences, Fundraising or a related field. Candidates with a degree in other disciplines with a proven relevant professional record will also be accepted.

· Work Experience
Essential
- Minimum Two (2) years of relevant working experience for high school diploma and One (1) year of experience with a bachelor’s degree or equivalent or higher.
- Ability to produce high-quality written materials tailored to specific audiences.
- Ability to balance different and sometimes competing needs and deadlines
- Experience in coordinating multiple stakeholders, with an ability to multi-task, manage time, and thrive in a high-pressure environment
- Experience working in a multi-cultural environment.
- Knowledge of partnerships, fundraising, and/or relationships with donors and/or external partners, and/or marketing and communications.

· Key Competencies
- Knowledge of humanitarian programming and/or UNHCR programmes and operational arrangements
- Knowledge of SharePoint 365 platform
- Experience in marketing and/or communications.
- Proficiency in MS office including MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
- Knowledge of CRM tools, ideally Salesforce
- Experience in a UN field location and/or working in a developing country.
- Proficiency in written and spoken Chinese (Cantonese and Putonghua) and English.

Responsibilities:
- As delegated by the supervisor, support the engagement of PPH donors, and all activities relevant for the acquisition and strengthening of relationships with them, depending on the local market and philanthropic landscape.
Support the preparation of pitches, presentations, proposals, reports and any other fundraising materials targeting PPH donors.
- Support the PPH team/colleagues in maintaining and managing the PPH prospect and donor pipeline, including support to the management of existing partnerships, e.g. by helping to draft donor reports, plan donor missions or other tasks necessary to ensure that relationships are appropriately nurtured.
- Support the team with desk and market research to provide intelligence to inform PPH initiatives and/or the approach to specific donors or sectors.
- Support on the logistics for internal and external events, including internal skill-shares.
- As delegated, and in collaboration with administrative colleagues, support PPH colleagues with procurement and administrative matters.
- Help to update content on PSP’s SharePoint platform, in order to improve internal communications, and to maintain a regular flow of information with colleagues within and outside PSP.
- Support PPH colleagues with information management and knowledge-sharing, through the collation and dissemination of documents and data pertaining to partnerships and philanthropy.
- Keep records of partnerships and relationships up to date. This might include helping to keep track of income raised, keeping internal calendars and plans updated, and supporting on data entry and maintenance on Salesforce.
- Gather and collate data/information on various topics and for specific audiences in support of communication and visibility plans with PPH donors, organize the logistics of content-gathering missions.
- Support the implementation of activities for UNHCR campaigns, including local and global UNHCR campaigns for PPH donors;
- Support the PPH team/colleagues in the adaptation, testing and/or development of activities and tools that support private sector fundraising efforts, including online activities in the future.
- Keep aware of developments in the fundraising and business environment and raise relevant updates on possible PPH opportunities with the supervisor.
- Perform other related duties as required.

Closing date: 11 November 2026

If you wish to be considered for this vacancy, please go to the link as below for application (https://unhcr.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/External/job/Senior-PPH-Assistant_JR2668764?locations=113ac21cb9f410123442ebb649210000).

The appointment offer will be subject to the proof of medical clearance and satisfactory reference checks.
Only shortlisted candidates will be notified and invited for the interview and written test.

job.title: Manager, Marketing, Partnerships & Fundraising
job.description:
Since 2017, Mighty Oaks Foundation has actively connected elderly care partners with schools through diverse arts programmes and creative initiatives, building bridges between old and young. Through shared learning experiences, elders are energised by youth, while young people gain respect and understanding for older generations. 

To date, the Foundation has benefited over 62,000 seniors and 36,000 students and has partnered with more than 150 elderly care organisations and over 100 schools, contributing to a more inclusive and caring community.  

The role 
Job title: Manager, Marketing, Partnerships & Fundraising
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
Direct report: Assistant Manager, Marketing & Events
Location: Hong Kong 

We are looking for a Manager, Marketing, Partnerships & Fundraising to build Mighty Oaks Foundation's profile, relationships and income. You will work with the CEO to shape the Foundation's marketing and communications direction, lead its implementation, develop partnerships, and support the growth and sustainability of our fundraising. 

You will carry an annual income target and manage the donor pipeline in support of the CEO.  

What you will do 
Marketing and communications 
• Work with the CEO to set the overall direction for the Foundation's marketing and communications, and lead the implementation of related plans and activities across PR, advertising, and internal and external communications. 
• Develop and deliver the annual marketing and communications plan, aligned with the Foundation's strategy. 
• Oversee Mighty Oaks Foundation's content calendar across all communications channels, ensuring timely, coordinated and consistent messaging. 
• Oversee the website upgrade, social media, newsletters and other owned channels, ensuring consistent brand and message in Chinese and English. 
• Manage media relations and build the Foundation's public profile. 
• Lead internal communications so that staff, volunteers and the Board are informed and engaged. 
• Support and implement corporate-related programmes and other initiatives under Mighty Oaks Foundation's Community and Advocacy pillar, including one-off engagements. 

Partnerships 
• Develop and manage partnerships with corporates, international schools, foundations, funders and other special partners not covered by the Programmes team. 
• Identify and secure new partners that extend the Foundation's reach, resources and impact.
• Oversee corporate volunteering programmes, working closely with the CEO on proposals and Head of Programmes on delivery. 
• Manage partner relationships end to end: proposals, agreements, recognition and reporting.  

Fundraising and donor engagement 
• Support the CEO in developing the Foundation's fundraising strategy. 
• Deliver an agreed annual income target. 
• Manage and grow the donor pipeline, bringing in new donors through prospect research, cultivation, asks and follow-up. 
• Lead donor engagement and stewardship, including acknowledgements, updates and impact reporting. 
• Lead the scoping and implementation of a new CRM system for the donor database and ensure donor and partner records are accurate and up to date.  

Fundraising events 
• Organise and host the Foundation's key fundraising events throughout the year. 
• Plan each event's concept, budget, sponsorship and guest list, and oversee delivery on the day. 
• Support programme events, including symposiums, graduation and seminars, and coordinate Mighty Oaks Foundation's year-round events calendar.  

As part of a lean team 
• Manage and develop the Assistant Manager, Marketing & Events. 
• Manage the marketing, partnerships and events budgets. 
• Establish and track key performance indicators across marketing, partnerships, fundraising and events, and prepare regular performance and impact reports for the CEO, funder and Board. 
• Provide cover for other roles when needed. 
• Uphold our safeguarding standards for seniors and students.  

What we are looking for 
Essential 
• Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, business administration or a related discipline. 
• At least five years' relevant experience across marketing, communications, partnerships or fundraising.  
• Track record of meeting income or business development targets. 
• Experience building and managing relationships with corporate partners, donors or sponsors, with a good existing network that can help expand our partnership and donor base. 
• Experience planning and delivering events, including fundraising, school and elderly events. 
• Strong media and PR skills, with excellent writing in Chinese and English. 
• Experience managing staff and budgets. 
• Confident user of digital and AI tools, including social media, digital marketing and donor or contact databases. 
• Hold a valid Sexual Conviction Record Check (SCRC) result, or be willing to complete the required check as a condition of employment. 
• Fluent in spoken Cantonese and English, and in written Traditional Chinese and English. 
• This role requires regular weekend and out-of-hours work to support events and engagements. Compensatory leave will be provided in accordance with the Foundation's policy.  

Preferred 
• Previous experience in an NGO or the social service sector. 
• Experience managing external PR, advertising and media agencies. 
• Experience with corporate volunteering or corporate social responsibility programmes. 
• Experience with major donors or high-net-worth giving. 
• Hands-on experience delivering fundraising campaigns, including donor cultivation, sponsorship development and income-generating initiatives. 
• Familiarity with elderly services, education or arts-based programmes.  

Who you are 
• Hands-on. Comfortable doing the work yourself in a small team, from writing a press release to running an event on the day. 
• Can-do. Positive, resourceful and solutions-focused when priorities shift. 
• Collaborative. You work easily across teams and share credit. 
• Sociable and well-networked. Outgoing, warm and credible. You enjoy meeting people and building relationships with donors, partners and media. 
• Results-driven. Motivated by targets and accountable for delivering them. 
• Engaging communicator. A confident presenter who communicates the Foundation's work clearly and persuasively, inspiring audiences to support and champion its mission. 
• Creative with strong visual judgement. You bring fresh, practical ideas and a strong sense of design and aesthetics to communications, campaigns and events. 
• Mission-driven. You care about elder dignity, intergenerational connection and emotional wellbeing.  

How to apply 
Please send your CV and a cover letter, with your expected salary and availability, to hr@mightyoaks.org . Please quote "Manager, Marketing, Partnerships & Fundraising" in the subject line. Personal data collected will be treated in strict confidence and used for recruitment purposes only. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Director of Development and Corporate Partnerships
job.description:
At ConnectedGroup, we are supporting an international non-profit organization dedicated to education, advocacy and conservation, in the search for their Director of Development and Corporate Partnerships.

Reporting into the CEO and leading a sizeable team (18 – 22 individuals), the DoD will be responsible to drive fundraising growth, strengthen corporate partnerships, and expand donor engagement. The role leads the development function while working closely with internal and external stakeholders to support the organisation's long-term mission and financial sustainability.

Responsibilities
·        Develop and deliver fundraising and partnership strategies that support sustainable revenue growth and diversify income streams.
·        Lead fundraising efforts across corporate partnerships, trusts and foundations, individual giving, major donors, sponsorships, and other philanthropic channels.
·        Strengthen and grow supporter engagement programmes, including individual giving and face-to-face fundraising activities.
·        Identify, develop, and secure new funding opportunities through corporate partners, foundations, high-net-worth individuals, and strategic collaborations.
·        Build and maintain relationships with senior corporate leaders, donors, foundations, and key external stakeholders, including identifying opportunities for deeper partnerships.
·        Engage confidently with C-suite stakeholders and decision-makers to secure support and develop long-term partnerships.
·        Work closely with programme teams to align donor interests with organisational priorities and ensure funding supports meaningful impact.
·        Lead fundraising campaigns, partnership initiatives, sponsorship activities, and donor engagement events.
·        Oversee key donor and corporate portfolios, ensuring high-quality stewardship and long-term relationship management.
·        Manage budgets, forecasts, fundraising performance, and team objectives.
·        Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team, fostering collaboration across fundraising, programme, education, and other specialist functions.
·        Represent the organisation externally with partners, donors, corporate leaders, and industry networks.

Requirements
  • Bachelors degree in a relevant field
  • Significant experience in fundraising, partnership development, philanthropy, business development, or a related leadership role.
  • Broad fundraising experience across multiple income streams, with strong knowledge of corporate fundraising, trusts and foundations, and individual giving. Experience with face-to-face fundraising would be particularly valuable.
  • Established network of corporate, trust, and foundation contacts, with China market exposure or relationships with China-based enterprises listed in Hong Kong considered an advantage.
  • Proven ability to develop strategic partnerships, secure funding, and deliver revenue growth.
  • Experience managing relationships with senior stakeholders, including board members, donors, executives, and corporate leaders.
  • Comfortable engaging and influencing C-suite stakeholders and navigating complex partnership discussions.
  • Experience with major donor fundraising is desirable, although direct ownership of major gifts may be shared with senior leadership.
  • Strong people leadership skills, with the ability to manage specialists, build collaboration, and bring together teams with different areas of expertise.
  • Commercially minded, with experience managing budgets, targets, and performance metrics.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management, and presentation skills in Cantonese, Mandarin and English.
  • Able to balance donor expectations with organisational and programme priorities.

Interested candidates please click on Apply, kindly note only relevant parties will be contacted.

job.title: Assistant Programme Officer (3 days a week)
job.description:
CantoGather is a Christian-affiliated charity founded in 2021. We work inside Hong Kong primary schools, bringing non-Chinese children, their Chinese peers and their parents together through Cantonese and intercultural learning.

Assistant Programme Officer (3 days a week)
HK$12,000 to HK$13,800 a month · 3 days a week · from November 2026

Help build a Hong Kong where every neighbour belongs! Join our small, warm and fun team to plan, teach and run real projects in primary schools. Things move fast here, so you’ll need to pick things up quickly.

Pay HK$12,000 to HK$13,800 a month plus MPF (HK$20,000 to HK$23,000 full-time equivalent)
Days Mon, Wed and Thu in person, 24 hours a week in total. It’s project-based, so you can move some of those hours to off-days for quick follow-ups.
Where Our Central office or partner schools. No work from home during probation.
Contract To 31 July 2027, renewable; 3-month probation
Start From November 2026
Reports to Senior Programme Manager

What you’ll do
• Plan lessons: write and adapt lesson plans and activities.
• Run CCC: manage our volunteer Cantonese tutors and the admin behind them.
• Teach: lead From Me to We sessions and our parent Cantonese classes.
• Work with schools: agree schedules and keep teachers in the loop.
• Keep things moving: messages, records and session set-up (yes, carrying boxes too).
A typical week: school sessions, lesson planning and volunteer coordination, with regular check-ins with your manager. The rest of the week is mostly yours.

You’ll fit right in if you’re
• Supportive: you’ve got the team’s back, just as we’ve got yours.
• Present: we know we can count on you, and find you when we need to.
• Focused: you know what matters and get it done.
• Excellent: you own your work and hold it to a high standard.
• Open: you pick things up fast and welcome feedback.

All rooted in our We CARE values: Creative & Curious, Authentic & Aware, Resilient & Responsible, Energetic & Engaging.

You’ll need
• 2 to 3 years’ work experience, especially teaching or working with people
• Fluent Cantonese and English, plus good written Chinese
• Willingness to represent and share our Christian mission and values
• Google Workspace, Microsoft Word, Excel and Canva
• Every Monday, Wednesday and Thursday free

Nice to have: teaching children Cantonese as a second language; Urdu, Hindi, Nepali, Tagalog or Punjabi.

We warmly welcome applicants of every ethnic background. If you’ve grown up between cultures in Hong Kong, that’s a real strength here.

What you’ll get
• Work that matters: help non-Chinese children feel they belong at school.
• Real ownership: run your own projects from day one, with a team that’s got your back.
• A wide skill set: teaching, lesson design, volunteer management and school partnerships, all in one role.
• Support along the way: regular check-ins with your manager, and space to try your own ideas.
• Balance: three days a week, with the rest of your week mostly yours.
• Grow with us: be part of an exciting, growing start-up, and help shape what comes next.

How to apply
Email your CV and a one-page note to recruitment@cantogather.com (subject: “Assistant Programme Officer”). Tell us why CantoGather, and one thing you ran from start to finish. Shortlisted applicants send a short video intro, then come for an interview. We’d love to hear from you!
Personal data will be used for recruitment only.

job.title: Legal Officer/ Manager
job.description:
We're looking for a dedicated Legal Officer with a passion for social justice to join our team in Hong Kong. This is a crucial role that combines legal expertise with project coordination and stakeholder engagement, focusing on advancing access to justice for migrant workers. If you're a proactive legal professional ready to make a tangible impact, we encourage you to apply.

This unique opportunity allows you to contribute to a mission-driven organisation, working at the intersection of legal support, community empowerment, and strategic development.

Applicants with strong relevant experience and background may be considered for a
Legal Manager position.

Key Responsibilities
1. Legal Casework Management
● Manage cross-border casework aligned with JWB’s mission
● Conduct outreach activities to raise awareness of JWB’s cross-border casework programme
● Support case team’s efforts in knowledge management and casework processes optimisation

2. Stakeholder Engagement & Communications
● Build and maintain collaborative relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, including law firms, NGOs, government agencies, and academic institutions
● Assist in content creation for communications materials, such as newsletters, social media posts, and website updates, to showcase our impact
● Manage volunteers to further JWB’s mission

3. Organisational Support
● Assist in writing grant proposals and preparing timely, accurate reports for funders
● As part of a small and agile team, provide flexible support to other organisational needs as they arise

Qualifications & Experience
1. Qualifications
● Bachelor of Law degree, or relevant degree/experience
● A minimum of 2 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in the non-profit sector, legal services, or a related field
● Language requirements: English and Chinese (Cantonese)
● Must have the right to live and work in Hong Kong

2. Personal attributes
● Passionate about improving the conditions of migrant workers
● Strong interpersonal skills and can work effectively and respectfully in a culturally diverse environment
● Willingness to take initiative and adapt to evolving challenges
● Self-directed and able to follow through on tasks and responsibilities independently

Terms of engagement
● Full-time
● 15 days paid annual leave, in addition to public holidays
● Remuneration:
○ Legal Officer: HKD19,500 – 22,500 per month
○ Legal Manager: HKD 23,000 – 26,000 per month
● Occasional overseas travel may be required as part of our work
● Professional development and coaching opportunities included

How to Apply
Are you ready to build a world where justice has no borders?

Please send your CV/resume and a cover letter to celine@forjusticewithoutborders.org with the subject line: “Application: Legal Officer – [Your Name]”. job.title: Development & Fundraising Officer
job.description:
Enrich is the leading Hong Kong charity promoting the economic empowerment of migrant domestic workers.

The Development & Fundraising Officer, reporting to the Development Manager, supports fundraising, donor relations, and campaign coordination to expand Enrich's educational programs and advance its mission. The primary objective is to help secure funding and build donor partnerships. The Development & Fundraising Officer will help research and write grants, coordinate impact monitoring and reporting, support campaigns and events, and track grant finances.

Job Overview
● Role: Development & Fundraising Officer (Part-Time, 3-4 days a week)
● Sector: Non-Profit / Financial Literacy
● Reporting To: Development Manager
● Objective: Support fundraising, donor relations, and campaign coordination to expand Enrich's mission.

Core Responsibilities
Grant Research & Writing Support
● Research Opportunities: Assist in identifying and researching funding opportunities with foundations and corporate partners aligned with Enrich's mission.
● Draft Applications: Help draft application materials, proposals, and project outcome summaries under the guidance of the Development Manager.
● Handle Administration: Support vital development administration, including preparing donor acknowledgement letters and donation receipts.

Impact Monitoring & Reporting
● Gather Feedback: Collaborate with the programmes team to gather qualitative and quantitative feedback, photos, evidence, and powerful impact stories from programme participants.
● Draft Reports: Assist in drafting accurate, compelling progress reports for funders that clearly demonstrate project outcomes and social return.

Campaigns & Event Coordination
● Support Communications: Support communication efforts for the Individual Giving programme, including writing thank-you acknowledgements and drafting engaging updates for donors.
● Coordinate Events: Help coordinate fundraising events, corporate employee engagement activities, and Enrich's participation in external functions.
● Manage CRM Data: Manage corporate volunteer sign-ups and maintain clean, up-to-date records in our CRM database to support seamless relationship management.

Track Grant Finances
● Ensure Compliance: Ensure restricted funds are spent according to grant requirements.

Position Requirements
Experience & Education
● Educational Background: A degree in Marketing, Public Relations, Business Administration, Non-Profit Management, or a related field.
● Professional Experience: Professional or practical experience in sales, marketing, communications, or fundraising preferred.

Technical & Soft Skills
● Passion & Values: Anchored in personal integrity and a strong sense of empathy, championing the financial empowerment and rights of migrant domestic workers in Hong Kong.
● Communication: Fluent in written and spoken English; Chinese language skills are a strong plus.
● Technical & Digital Literacy: Competent IT skills, including MS Office Suite, Google Workspace, and familiarity with AI tools, with basic graphic design capabilities (e.g., Canva or Adobe) and/or website content management experience as distinct advantages.
● Work Style: Detail-oriented, highly organized, and eager to learn; combines the ability to drive results independently during remote workdays with active, enthusiastic participation in collaborative team settings.

Salary and benefits:
Salary: HKD 11,000 - 12,000 a month, working part-time, 3.5 days per week
We offer annual leave, health insurance, and contributions to the Mandatory Provident Fund. Other staff benefits include an Employee Assistance Program that offers up to 4 free counselling sessions. We are a learning organisation and offer development and well-being opportunities throughout the year. We currently have a hybrid working model in place, allowing flexibility in working locations within Hong Kong.

Enrich is a signatory to the Racial Diversity and Inclusion Charter of the Equal Opportunities Commission.

How to apply:
All interested applicants should send a full resume and a cover letter expressing interest in the role and detailing how your skills suit this role to joanne@enrichhk.org by 16th October 2026. Unfortunately, due to the anticipated high volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Personal data collected will be used for recruitment purposes only. Applications are welcome until the position is filled.

job.title: Data Analyst (Measurement, Evaluation and Learning)
job.description:
Bei Shan Tang Foundation is a private philanthropic foundation founded in 1985 to enhance global understanding of Chinese culture through traditional art and art history. Alongside this mission, since 2014 we have committed significant resources to transforming education in Hong Kong through Positive Education — cultivating resilience, inspiration, and collaborative communities grounded in evidence-based practices. 

We empower students to embrace change, thrive, and lead purpose-driven lives. Through collaborations with schools and esteemed institutions locally and worldwide, we introduce pedagogical innovations and effective strategies for educators. We also provide scholarships for students with financial needs to pursue studies abroad, nurturing Hong Kong’s next generation of leaders.

The role
Reporting to the Director (Education), you will serve as the Foundation’s quantitative expert — ensuring our education initiatives are grounded in rigorous evidence and our impact is clearly understood. You will own the full data cycle: from designing measurement approaches and managing longitudinal datasets through statistical analysis, interpretation, and translating findings into clear insights for diverse audiences. While you will work independently on technical analyses, you will collaborate closely with colleagues to ensure every analysis addresses meaningful questions that matter for students, educators, and the Foundation’s mission.

Key responsibilities
Measurement and insight generation
  • Design for understanding: Translate research and evaluation questions into appropriate quantitative measurement frameworks, adapting or developing tools that capture what matters in education and wellbeing initiatives.
  • Build the evidence base: Establish, maintain, and manage multi-wave and longitudinal datasets from the Foundation’s research, evaluation, and education programs, ensuring data quality and accessibility.
  • Analyze with rigor: Select and apply appropriate statistical methods — including descriptive statistics, psychometric analysis, group comparisons, regression, and longitudinal modeling — based on research questions, measurement characteristics, and data structure.
  • Uncover what matters: Identify meaningful patterns, trends, and findings that support continuous improvement of the Foundation’s education and wellbeing programs.

Communication and impact
  • Translate complexity: Prepare clear summaries of analytical findings across multiple formats — spreadsheets, tables, infographics, and written reports — ensuring technical accuracy without sacrificing accessibility.
  • Bridge worlds: Interpret statistical findings and communicate their implications and limitations clearly to non-technical colleagues, helping them make informed decisions.
  • Share learning: Contribute to deliverables that promote public awareness and engagement, including presentations, reports, and academic papers that advance the field.

You may also contribute to knowledge management within the Foundation and assist in facilitating education-related professional development offerings. 

Who you are
We value how you approach your work as much as what you know. The strongest candidates will recognize themselves in the following:
  • You believe data is a tool for positive change, not an end in itself. You are driven by curiosity about what helps students thrive and educators succeed.
  • You balance rigor with pragmatism. You apply sophisticated methods when they add value, but you also know when a simpler approach tells the story more clearly.
  • You are a careful listener and clear communicator. You ask questions to understand what colleagues truly need, and you explain complex findings in ways that empower rather than confuse.
  • You are systematic and detail-oriented, but you never lose sight of the bigger picture — the students and educators whose lives our programs touch.
  • You are intellectually honest. You report findings accurately, acknowledge limitations openly, and view unexpected results as opportunities to learn.
  • You are deeply curious about Hong Kong’s education system and genuinely motivated to contribute to its improvement. 

What you’ll bring
  • A bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Data Science, Psychology, Education, Social Sciences, or a related quantitative discipline (postgraduate qualification preferred).
  • 2–5 years of experience in data analysis, quantitative research, program evaluation, or educational/social research, with a track record of independently conducting rigorous analyses.
  • Strong proficiency in SPSS, R, or Python, with demonstrated ability to conduct descriptive statistics, psychometric analysis, group comparisons, regression, and longitudinal or repeatedmeasures analyses.
  • Solid understanding of research methodology, quantitative analysis, and measurement principles. Experience with multi-wave or longitudinal datasets is an advantage.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and systematic approach to data quality, statistical analysis, and interpretation.
  • Experience in data visualization and workflow automation is a strong asset.
  • Proficiency in English and Chinese; ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.

Terms and benefits
This is a one-year fixed-term contract, renewable based on mutual agreement and operational needs. We offer competitive remuneration commensurate with experience, a 5-day work week, compensatory leave for weekend work, compassionate leave, comprehensive medical and dental insurance, and annual health checkups.

How to apply
Bei Shan Tang Foundation is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Fresh graduates with relevant skills are encouraged to apply; experience in education and psychology is an advantage.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter indicating your earliest starting date and expected salary to Ms. Erica Yam (Senior Programme Manager) at ericayam@beishantang.org with “Application for Data Analyst (Measurement, Evaluation and Learning)” in the subject line.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Programs & Operations Manager / Director (Hong Kong)
job.description:
PILnet is an international, locally present non-governmental organization (NGO) that partners with legal professionals and social purpose organizations (SPOs) globally to protect civic space, address global challenges, and work to build just, equitable, and sustainable societies. PILnet does this by supporting civil society, engaging legal professionals, and nurturing the next generation of legal professionals in three strategic priority areas: civic space, climate justice, and people on the move. PILnet currently has offices in New York, Budapest, and Hong Kong, but operates globally.

PILnet Hong Kong works with SPOs, legal professionals, and law students to (i) strengthen the legal capacity and resilience of the social sector and (ii) strengthen pro bono culture in Hong Kong. PILnet Hong Kong’s main services for SPOs include its Pro Bono Clearinghouse and its Legal Health Check service. Through these services, PILnet Hong Kong connects SPOs with pro bono lawyers, helping them access high-quality legal expertise that would otherwise be out of reach. On strengthening pro bono culture, PILnet Hong Kong works closely with law students as the next generation of lawyers. Through providing mentorship, internships, and other learning opportunities, PILnet Hong Kong highlights the importance of public interest law and pro bono work, instilling in law students a long-term commitment to supporting the social sector. PILnet Hong Kong further strengthens pro bono culture by regularly convening lawyers, through events such as the Hong Kong Pro Bono Roundtables, to explore different ways in which they can support public interest causes. PILnet Hong Kong is guided by its Board of Directors, with half of its board members based in Hong Kong.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Based in Hong Kong and reporting to the Co-Executive Director, who is based in Asia, the Programs & Operations Manager/Director (Hong Kong) will oversee the design and execution of all projects in Hong Kong and ensure the smooth operations of the office. They will work with a team of legal officers and program staff, ensuring that the Hong Kong program remains relevant to local stakeholders and aligns with PILnet’s mission. They will also work closely with the rest of the PILnet team and other colleagues across PILnet’s offices to design and implement cross-border strategies and projects. The Programs & Operations Manager/Director (Hong Kong) will be responsible for the following areas:

Programs:
- Oversee the successful and timely implementation of projects focused on Hong Kong in accordance with relevant grants;
- Conduct team meetings to discuss regular project tasks and issues;
- In consultation with the Co-Executive Director and the development team, investigate and explore new opportunities that align with PILnet’s vision and strategy;
- Keep the Co-Executive Director updated on developments related to Hong Kong programs and staff matters; and
- Coordinate sessions and other activities in preparation of PILnet’s annual Global Forum held in a different city each year.

Partnerships:
- In consultation with the development team, manage, deepen, and strengthen relationships with Hong Kong based funders;
- Support the Co-Executive Director and the development team in writing grant proposals, financial reports, donor reports, and other reports as necessary;
- Build partnerships with local stakeholders, such as public interest law organizations, government, corporations, and universities; and
- Represent PILnet at external events.

Legal, Governance and Finance:
- Ensure that the Hong Kong program operations and activities adhere to internal policies;
- In consultation with the Global Senior Counsel, support the Co-Executive Director in ensuring that PILnet Hong Kong is compliant with relevant laws and regulations;
- In consultation with the Global Senior Counsel, review agreements with external vendors, suppliers, and partners, including law firms and foundations, as necessary;
- Support the Co-Executive Director in managing and documenting PILnet Hong Kong board meetings; and
- Support the Co-Executive Director in reviewing and executing financial transactions of the Hong Kong office, as reviewed and approved by the finance team.

People Management:
- Manage and collaborate with a team of legal officers, program officers, fellows, and interns, to provide guidance, input, and feedback;

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS
• Degree in law, political science, international relations, public administration or related field. Preference will be given to applicants with a law degree.

• 8-10 years of relevant work experience, preferably in the legal nonprofit or public interest law field, and/or a graduate degree in a relevant field combined with relevant experience. Candidates with less relevant experience will be considered as Managers.

• Project management experience and a record of delivering projects on time and to budget.
• Proactive, creative and opportunity-driven mindset.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, demonstrated by the ability to present effectively and persuasively.
• Excellent people skills, including networking, organizing, negotiating, and inspiring.
• Strong ability to delegate tasks effectively and mentor program staff, fellows and interns.

LOCATION & CONDITIONS
You will work alongside a small multicultural team from nonprofit management and legal backgrounds, providing you with a supportive and flexible working environment. The nature of the position mandates that the prospective candidate is based and has the right to work in the Hong Kong SAR. PILnet is not in a position to facilitate working visas and work permits.
This is a full-time position or a part-time (min. 60% capacity) position. The position will involve some regional and international travel, essential to the implementation of PILnet’s activities. It is not expected to be more than 15 days per year cumulatively.
